During extrusion many fine b phase particles with an irregular morphology were dynamically precipitated at the boundaries of recrystallized grains (Fig. 1a). The volume fraction and the average size of the b phase particles were 0.13 and 0.91 lm (distributed in the size range 0.5–1.5 lm), respectively.

Many spherical particles measuring /C24 50–100 nm are dispersed in the grain interiors (also shown in the inset to Fig. 2a). The EDS and TEM microdiffraction analyses confirmed that the particles are Mg17(Al,Zn)12 phase and are not crystallographically related to the matrix.
The HRDSR 3SP sheet (Fig. 3a) consists of spherical b particles measuring /C24 50–100 nm, but most of these particles are located near the grain boundaries.
The microstructure of aged HRDSR 3SP shows very fine particles additionally precipitated in the grain interiors (Fig. 3b).
The average grain sizes of the as-extruded material and the HRDSR 2SP sheet, which were determined based on the SEM images obtained, were 3.4 and 0.8 lm, respectively.
The average grain size measured by SEM was 0.6 lm, which is smaller than that of the HRDSR 2SP sheet.

From Figure 4b it is obvious that fracture occurred before neck formation in HRDSR 2SP. This may be due to the presence of non-fully refined elongated b phase in the matrix, causing the formation of microcracks.
Some dislocations are attached to the particles (marked A, B and C), providing evidence for interactions between dislocations and particles.
This result indicates the importance of the presence of a high volume fraction of nano-sized b particles in grain interiors for enhanced strain hardening.
The current SEM and TEM observations indicates that separation of the nanosized b phase particles from the elongated b phase first requires the formation of nanosized (sub)grains within it.

The small non-uniform deformation of aged HRDSR 3SP may be a result of the presence of small particles in the grain interiors that decreases the strain rate sensitivity by behaving as athermal obstacles to dislocation glide [20].
